C1.recordedClaim: A violated constraint reverts the judge call. Guarded actions roll back only when assertions execute mandatorily in the same transaction and the enclosing executor propagates failure. `assertBatch` evaluates entries in order and stops at the first failure.

C2.recordedClaim: `assertParam` resolves one `InputParam` through its fetcher and validates its inline constraints

C4.recordedClaim: `assertBatch` entries without a TARGET are predicate entries: resolve and validate only, no call

C5.recordedClaim: For a nonzero TARGET, the constructed staticcall sends functionSig followed by CALL_DATA values in order; target position does not change that layout.

C6.recordedClaim: A TARGET resolving to `address(0)` skips the constructed call

C7.recordedClaim: View-mode refusals: outputParams `OutputParamsNotSupported(entry)`, VALUE `ValueParamNotSupported(entry,param)`, second TARGET `DuplicateTargetParam(entry)`, BALANCE target `BalanceCannotBeTarget(entry,param)`

C8.recordedClaim: A TARGET word with dirty upper bytes reverts `InvalidAddressWord(paramIndex, word)`

C9.recordedClaim: `ConstraintFailed` carries message, entry index, param index, constraint index, kind, actual word and echoed reference

C10.recordedClaim: Every judge function has a custom-message overload echoed in `ConstraintFailed`; defaults are "PARAM", "COMPOSABLE", and "" on primitive operands

C11.recordedClaim: A reverting constructed batch call reverts `CallFailed(target, builtCalldata)`; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C12.recordedClaim: Call-based fetchers and constructed calls use STATICCALL; literals and native balances are read directly, with no storage writes.

C13.recordedClaim: A STATIC_CALL operand can invoke `assertBatch`, allowing validity, fallback and revert probes over a batch.

C15.recordedClaim: STATIC_CALL resolution preserves raw returndata bytes after constraints; other caller/gas contexts may produce different values.

C16.recordedClaim: A STATIC_CALL to a code-less address reverts `CallFailed(target, callData)` instead of yielding empty data

C17.recordedClaim: A reverting STATIC_CALL target reverts `CallFailed(target, data)`; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C18.recordedClaim: BALANCE: 40-byte `token ++ account`; token 0 reads the native balance, else `balanceOf` first word; other lengths `InvalidBalanceData(entry,param,len)`

C19.recordedClaim: A failure inside a nested STATIC_CALL surfaces as `CallFailed` in the resolving frame (inner reason lost); exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C20.recordedClaim: Malformed STATIC_CALL `paramData` can produce ABI-decoder bare reverts; decoder allocation panics and resource failures remain possible.

C21.recordedClaim: `resolve` validates constraints before returning; a violation reverts `ConstraintFailed("",0,0,..)`, making any node an inline assert

C22.recordedClaim: STATIC_CALL operands can nest core primitives into finite trees; each call has its own caller and gas context.

C23.recordedClaim: `gather` returns raw operand results as canonical `bytes[]`; element contents remain untyped until a consumer validates them.

C24.recordedClaim: `gather` and `get` resolve each supplied operand once; duplicated entries are independent operands.

C25.recordedClaim: `gather` names a failing operand by its list index

C26.recordedClaim: `gather`'s result feeds a `bytes[]` position of `get` as one whole argument

C27.recordedClaim: `pick` selects a full raw word, with negative indices counted from the end; invalid indices raise `ReturnDataOutOfBounds(index,length)`.

C28.recordedClaim: After successful resolution, an empty `nav` path returns the bytes unchanged without checking the descriptor.

C29.recordedClaim: Static `nav` terminals return their complete bare ABI footprint after bounds and word-range checks.

C30.recordedClaim: Every static word returned by `nav` must satisfy its descriptor range; failures report `InvalidValue` at the resolved-data offset.

C31.recordedClaim: Only the returned value is checked; siblings the path skips are not

C32.recordedClaim: A string/bytes terminal returns `[0x20][len][payload]`; nonzero padding reverts `InvalidValue` at the first dirty byte

C33.recordedClaim: Dynamic array/tuple terminals return canonical single-value ABI encoding; malformed selected nested values raise codec errors.

C34.recordedClaim: Arrays of static elements return `[0x20][len][elements]`, bounds- and range-checked in place

C35.recordedClaim: `nav` indexes tuple components nonnegatively and array elements with signed indices; index errors follow descriptor/data validation order.

C36.recordedClaim: A step into a non-composite reverts `InvalidNavigation(descriptor position)`

C37.recordedClaim: Ordinary nonempty `nav` selection returns canonical encoding of the declared terminal; parent offsets, skipped siblings and sentinels have weaker validation.

C38.recordedClaim: Nonempty navigation parses the complete descriptor before reading data; malformed syntax raises `InvalidTypeDescriptor`, subject to arithmetic/resource limits.

C39.recordedClaim: Navigation supports finite recursive tuples and arrays when intermediate arithmetic, gas, stack and memory suffice.

C40.recordedClaim: `LEN` (`int256.min`) as last entry returns the decoded length: element count, or byte length for string/bytes

C41.recordedClaim: `LEN` rejects static values and empty prefixes. For unsupported dynamic tuples/fixed arrays, a truncated selected word can fail before `InvalidNavigation`.

C42.recordedClaim: `LEN` checks padded bytes or array heads fit; it does not validate array tails, narrow element ranges or byte padding contents.

C43.recordedClaim: `PAYLOAD` (`int256.min + 1`) returns the raw string/bytes payload, exact length, unpadded; an outer nav re-enters it

C44.recordedClaim: `PAYLOAD` accepts only bytes/string after a nonempty prefix; other terminal kinds raise `InvalidNavigation` before reading a length.

C45.recordedClaim: A `PAYLOAD` length overrunning the data reverts `ReturnDataOutOfBounds`; nothing past the data is read

C46.recordedClaim: Nonfinal LEN/PAYLOAD sentinels undergo ordinary navigation checks and cannot select a valid element.

C47.recordedClaim: Navigation may fail on checked arithmetic or exhausted gas/stack/memory; no unconditional no-panic or no-exhaustion guarantee applies.

C48.recordedClaim: `chain`: `start` resolves to a clean address; each non-final hop returns the next target in its first word; the final returndata passes through raw

C49.recordedClaim: `chain` dirty address words revert `InvalidAddressWord` (0 for start, hop index + 1 mid-chain)

C51.recordedClaim: A mid-chain hop returning under 32 bytes reverts `ReturnDataOutOfBounds`

C52.recordedClaim: A failing hop reverts `CallFailed(target, hopCalldata)`, identifying the exact hop; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C53.recordedClaim: `read` sends `selector ++` each segment's full resolved bytes, in order, to the resolved target and returns raw returndata

C54.recordedClaim: `read`, `get` and `chain` require a clean target word: dirty upper bytes revert `InvalidAddressWord(0, word)`

C55.recordedClaim: `read`/`get` revert `CallFailed` on a code-less target or a reverting constructed call; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C56.recordedClaim: `read`/`get` name operands as target 0 and args at index + 1

C57.recordedClaim: The destination sees the core as `msg.sender` (`read`, `get`, `chain`)

C58.recordedClaim: `get` constructs canonical ABI arguments from the declared descriptor and resolved component values; unknown names retain unrestricted-word semantics.

C59.recordedClaim: `get` reverts with codec errors naming the argument (`ComponentCountMismatch`, `InvalidComponentEnvelope`, `InvalidComponentLength`, `InvalidComponentValue`) and `InvalidTypeDescriptor`

C60.recordedClaim: `get` with `"()"` and no args calls the bare selector

C62.recordedClaim: `cond` is lazy: the losing branch is never resolved

C63.recordedClaim: `cond` truth is the first word nonzero; under 32 bytes reverts `ReturnDataOutOfBounds(0,len)`

C64.recordedClaim: The winning branch is resolved with its constraints and returned byte-identically

C65.recordedClaim: A violated condition constraint reverts the whole `cond`; operands are 0 (condition), 1 (then), 2 (else)

C66.recordedClaim: `orElse` returns the attempt on success or resolves the fallback on an ordinary failure; exhaustion classification propagates `SubcallOutOfGas`.

C67.recordedClaim: The fallback resolves in-frame, its failures propagate, and it is operand 1

C68.recordedClaim: `orElse(a, orElse(b, c))` tries sources in order; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C69.recordedClaim: Failed calls classify reserved exact four-byte `SubcallOutOfGas` or remaining gas <= gasBefore/63 as exhaustion. The marker is unauthenticated, near-exhausting reverts may be refused, and external targets can hide failures.

C70.recordedClaim: `isValid` reports successful resolution and constraints, not returned boolean truth; ordinary failure yields 0, exhaustion classification propagates.

C71.recordedClaim: `isValid(revertData(a,selector))` reflects the probe rules, including zero-selector/code-less acceptance and the exhaustion exception.

C72.recordedClaim: `revertData`: zero selector returns the whole revert data; a nonzero one must match and is stripped; mismatch or under 4 bytes reverts `UnexpectedRevertData(expected, actual or 0)`; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C73.recordedClaim: `revertData` over a succeeding call reverts `DidNotRevert(target, callData)`

C74.recordedClaim: `revertData` refuses a non-STATIC_CALL operand (`RevertProbeNotACall(fetcherType)`) and a constrained one (`RevertProbeConstrained(count)`)

C75.recordedClaim: `revertData` on a code-less target: zero selector returns empty data, a nonzero one reverts `UnexpectedRevertData(sel, 0)`

C76.recordedClaim: `revertData` calls in-frame so the direct target's revert reason survives; a nested core primitive reports the core's own error; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

C77.recordedClaim: Core failures may be declared errors, ABI-decoder bare reverts, checked panics or resource failures; selector-bearing failures are not universal.

C78.recordedClaim: The core has only view entrypoints, no storage writes, no payable entrypoint and no authorization or fund-management logic.

C82.recordedClaim: An unconstrained RAW_BYTES operand may be empty and still pass `assertParam`

C83.recordedClaim: A constructed batch call must succeed, but all its returndata is discarded, including encoded `false`

C84.recordedClaim: `isValid` reports successful resolution and inline constraints, not boolean truth of the returned value

A1.recordedClaim: Descriptors use nonempty `[a-z0-9]+` names/tuples and dynamic or positive fixed-array suffixes, subject to parser arithmetic/resource bounds.

A2.recordedClaim: `bytes` and `string` are the only dynamic base names; `T[]` and any tuple with a dynamic component are dynamic; every other name is one 32-byte word

A3.recordedClaim: Head footprint in words: 1 for a dynamic type, component sum for a static tuple, k times element footprint for a static `T[k]`

A4.recordedClaim: Fixed lengths and static fixed-array footprints are at most `2^32-1`; bare tuple widths sum their components separately.

A5.recordedClaim: InvalidTypeDescriptor for an oversized length is raised "at the length" (the closing bracket, or the digit that crosses the bound)

A6.recordedClaim: `T[0]` is refused (as solc refuses to declare it), including `[00]` and `T[0]` nested inside a tuple; a leading zero before a nonzero digit is still a length

A7.recordedClaim: Every supported canonical value spans at least one ABI word; zero-width descriptors are rejected.

A8.recordedClaim: Malformed descriptors ordinarily raise `InvalidTypeDescriptor`; checked arithmetic and resource failures remain possible.

A9.recordedClaim: Codec traversal requires representable cursors and adequate execution resources; no unlimited-input no-panic guarantee applies.

A10.recordedClaim: Static words are held to their base name's range as solc's decoder does: uintN/address/bool high bits clear, intN sign-extended, bytesN/function low bits clear

A11.recordedClaim: The 256-bit names and names that are not well-formed narrow ABI types (`uint7`, `uint08`, `int1000`, `bytes0`, `foo`) admit every word

A12.recordedClaim: Range checks apply on every path: static elements of arrays, static components of dynamic tuples, static tuples nested in static tuples, fixed arrays (every copy), tuple components, words inside dynamic components

A13.recordedClaim: Canonical single-value encoding is the bare static footprint or `[0x20][body]` for a dynamic value, with tight offsets, clean padding and in-range words.

A14.recordedClaim: Offsets must be tight: every offset points exactly where the previous tail ended

A15.recordedClaim: bytes/string padding must be zero; a dirty padding byte reverts InvalidValue at that byte

A16.recordedClaim: Encoded lengths/counts are bounded before stride multiplication; descriptor/cursor arithmetic still requires representability.

A17.recordedClaim: Trailing bytes after the last tail are rejected (InvalidValue at their offset)

A18.recordedClaim: `packArray`/`pack` returns the canonical `abi.encode(T[])` of the values

A19.recordedClaim: `unpack` validates an encoded array and returns canonical elements; `pack` reconstructs the same canonical array under the codec size bounds.

A20.recordedClaim: `tupleLayout` requires a nonempty parenthesized tuple. Call constructors separately accept `()` with no arguments.

A21.recordedClaim: `tuple(t, args)` is the canonical ABI encoding of the tuple: static components copied verbatim, dynamic envelopes stripped with the true offset written, verbatim splicing correct at any nesting depth

A22.recordedClaim: ComponentCountMismatch when `args.length` differs from the component count

A23.recordedClaim: InvalidComponentLength(index, expected, actual) when a static component is not exactly its head footprint

A24.recordedClaim: InvalidComponentEnvelope(index, length, head) when a dynamic component is shorter than two words, unaligned, or not headed by 0x20

A25.recordedClaim: InvalidComponentValue(index, offset) for a malformed body or an out-of-range static word inside a component, with the codec's error rerouted through the caller's context

A26.recordedClaim: Codec error offsets identify a word start, dirty padding byte or expected consumed end, depending on the failed check.

A27.recordedClaim: InvalidCallbackResult routing: a Collections callback result not canonical for its declared type reverts InvalidCallbackResult(operation, index, other, target) via the Context

A28.recordedClaim: Canonical values of supported descriptors are accepted within the codec arithmetic and execution-resource bounds.

A29.recordedClaim: A shape-compatible but semantically wrong descriptor can reinterpret a value without rejection.

A34.recordedClaim: All four production contracts import AbiCodec; imported-source metadata changes affect their deployment bytecode.

W1.recordedClaim: ConstraintType IDs are EQ=0, GTE=1, LTE=2, IN=3, GTE_SIGNED=4, LTE_SIGNED=5, OR=6, SKIP=7, IN_SIGNED=8, identical to the Biconomy reference

W2.recordedClaim: The shared structs/enums use the ERC-8211 ABI wire layout; compatible predicate encodings decode without a private format extension.

W3.recordedClaim: InputParamType TARGET=0, VALUE=1, CALL_DATA=2; InputParamFetcherType RAW_BYTES=0, STATIC_CALL=1, BALANCE=2; OutputParamFetcherType EXEC_RESULT=0, STATIC_CALL=1

W4.recordedClaim: Constraint i checks complete resolved word i (positional semantics)

W5.recordedClaim: The same positions apply to STATIC_CALL and BALANCE fetchers; a BALANCE value is one word, so `[GTE(lo), LTE(hi)]` checks two words and reverts on a balance (use one IN for a scalar range)

W6.recordedClaim: Constrained positions are raw ABI words: a dynamic return starts with its offset, not its contents

W7.recordedClaim: Every constraint needs a complete word, SKIP included

W8.recordedClaim: All word bounds are checked before any predicate is evaluated (short data reverts `ReturnDataOutOfBounds(words, length)` even when an earlier predicate would fail)

W9.recordedClaim: EQ compares raw words; GTE and LTE compare unsigned; each takes exactly one 32-byte reference word

W10.recordedClaim: GTE_SIGNED / LTE_SIGNED reinterpret complete words as int256; signed constraints are supported at the wire boundary (the SDK may still lower through Operations)

W11.recordedClaim: IN and IN_SIGNED are inclusive ranges over `abi.encode(lo, hi)` (unsigned / signed)

W12.recordedClaim: A range whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound (under its signedness) reverts `InvalidConstraintRange(entry, param, constraint)`

W13.recordedClaim: SKIP takes empty referenceData and leaves its word unconstrained; a SKIP payload reverts `InvalidConstraintData`

W14.recordedClaim: Reference lengths are exact: 32 bytes for EQ/GTE/LTE/signed leaves, 64 for ranges, 0 for SKIP; anything else reverts `InvalidConstraintData(entry, param, constraint, length)`

W15.recordedClaim: Deliberate stricter rejection: IN / IN_SIGNED require exactly 64 bytes where Biconomy's decoder tolerates trailing bytes

W16.recordedClaim: Constraint acceptance preserves the reference predicate rules, with stricter exact range lengths and view-mode routing restrictions.

W17.recordedClaim: Canonical predicate constraints use the reference positional comparison, OR and SKIP rules.

W18.recordedClaim: OR (6) carries `abi.encode(Constraint[])` of non-OR leaves and passes when at least one leaf matches the same word

W19.recordedClaim: An empty OR reverts `InvalidOrConstraint(entry, param, constraint)`

W20.recordedClaim: A nested OR is rejected wherever it sits, before short-circuiting, even after a matching leaf

W21.recordedClaim: Non-OR leaves are evaluated in order and short-circuit on the first match (a malformed leaf before a match rejects; one after a match is never examined)

W22.recordedClaim: Malformed OR `referenceData` can produce ABI-decoder bare reverts; decoder allocation panics and resource failures remain possible.

W23.recordedClaim: An out-of-range ConstraintType (9..255) is never accepted and reverts without data

W24.recordedClaim: `ConstraintFailed` carries the assertion message, entry index, param index, constraint index, constraint kind, the actual word at that index and the reference data echoed as given

W25.recordedClaim: Every judge function has a custom-message overload whose message is reported in `ConstraintFailed`; the message is `""` when the constraint sits on a primitive's operand

W26.recordedClaim: `InvalidConstraintData`, `InvalidOrConstraint` and `InvalidConstraintRange` identify the entry, operand and outer constraint (word) index

W27.recordedClaim: Assertions does not implement `IComposableExecution`: the judge is a view function over the same encoding, not a payable executor

W28.recordedClaim: A predicate check encoded as an ERC-8211 predicate entry (no TARGET) passes through `assertBatch` unchanged and is judged as `assertParam` judges it

W29.recordedClaim: Constraints on primitive operands (`resolve`, graph Resolve nodes, etc.) use the same positional semantics as the judge

W30.recordedClaim: The reference-oracle fixture is pinned bytecode; fixture identity does not establish current public-chain code availability.

O1.recordedClaim: `add`/`sub`/`mul` (uint256 and int256) are checked: overflow or underflow reverts with Panic(0x11)

O2.recordedClaim: Unsigned `div`/`mod` truncate; zero divisor reverts with Panic(0x12)

O3.recordedClaim: Signed `div` truncates toward zero, `type(int256).min / -1` reverts Panic(0x11); signed `mod` takes the dividend's sign

O5.recordedClaim: Signed-base exponentiation checks every selected multiplication/square; success equals the integer power and intermediate overflow raises Panic(0x11).

O6.recordedClaim: `min`/`max` for both overloads (signed ordering on int256)

O7.recordedClaim: `absDiff` is total and never reverts; the int256 overload returns the exact uint256 distance even for int256.min to int256.max

O8.recordedClaim: Unsigned `mulDiv` uses the full 512-bit product and rounds once per `rounding` (Trunc = Floor, Ceil up); a result past uint256 reverts Panic(0x11)

O9.recordedClaim: `mulDiv` with a zero denominator reverts Panic(0x12) (both overloads, every rounding)

O10.recordedClaim: Signed `mulDiv`: magnitude 512-bit product, Trunc toward zero, Floor toward -inf, Ceil toward +inf, negative denominators and int256.min operands allowed, a rounded result outside int256 reverts Panic(0x11)

O11.recordedClaim: An out-of-range `Rounding` value is refused by the ABI decoder with a bare revert

O12.recordedClaim: Unsigned `addMod`/`mulMod` use the full 512-bit sum/product (EVM ADDMOD/MULMOD); zero modulus reverts Panic(0x12)

O13.recordedClaim: Signed `addMod`/`mulMod`: overflow-free intermediate; the remainder takes the sign of the mathematical sum/product, independent of m's sign

O14.recordedClaim: Signed `addMod`/`mulMod` support int256.min in every operand; zero modulus reverts Panic(0x12)

O15.recordedClaim: Unsigned `powMod` returns the modular power without intermediate power overflow; exponent zero yields `1 % m`, and m=0 raises Panic(0x12).

O16.recordedClaim: Exponents >= `2^32` try MODEXP; smaller exponents use MULMOD. The threshold is a policy, not a universal gas crossover.

O17.recordedClaim: Failed or non-32-byte MODEXP replies select the MULMOD fallback. A successful 32-byte reply is trusted to represent the precompile result.

O18.recordedClaim: Signed-base `powMod(int256,uint256,int256)`: power of abs(a) mod abs(m), negative iff a < 0 and the exponent is odd; modulus sign ignored; int256.min supported

O19.recordedClaim: Negative modular exponents require an inverse; failure reports the original base/modulus magnitudes, and modulus 1 yields zero.

O20.recordedClaim: `powMod(int256,int256,int256)`: signed base and signed exponent, sign rule "in either direction", magnitudes coprime for negative exponents

O22.recordedClaim: `log2` is floor(log2(x)) (bit length minus one); `LogarithmUndefined(0)` at 0

O23.recordedClaim: `rpow`: fixed-point binary exponentiation rounding down each step; 0^0 is one unit, 0^n is 0; Panic(0x11) on a scaled intermediate past uint256, Panic(0x12) for base 0

O24.recordedClaim: `rpow`'s final error is not bounded by the number of multiplies: rpow(19, 16, 10) = 276889 vs a single rounding's 288441

O26.recordedClaim: `expWad` executes a quantized rational approximation; x<=-42139678854452767551 yields zero, and x>=135305999368893231589 raises Panic(0x11).

O27.recordedClaim: `lnWad` executes a quantized rational approximation; nonpositive inputs raise `LogarithmUndefined(x)`.

O28.recordedClaim: Global real-function accuracy, monotonicity, positivity and exp/log inverse-error bounds are not established by the finite-word source specifications.

O29.recordedClaim: `eq`/`ne` (bit-level) and `lt`/`gt`/`le`/`ge` (both overloads) return bool, spliced as a 0/1 word

O31.recordedClaim: Unsigned shifts follow EVM semantics: shifts >=256 yield zero.

O32.recordedClaim: `shr(int256,uint256)` is SAR: rounds toward -inf; shifts of 256 or more yield 0 or -1 by sign

O33.recordedClaim: Sign-extension recipe `shr(int256(shl(x, 256 - bits)), 256 - bits)` re-widens a narrow two's-complement field

O34.recordedClaim: `bitSet(mask, index)`: indices past 255 are never set

O36.recordedClaim: `blockHash(n)`: BLOCKHASH semantics, 0 for the current block, the future and blocks older than 256

O37.recordedClaim: `codeHash`: EXTCODEHASH, 0 for a nonexistent account, keccak256("") for an existing code-less account

O38.recordedClaim: `blobHash(i)`: the versioned hash of blob i, zero when the tx carries none at i

O39.recordedClaim: `rawCall` is a raw staticcall: no selector, no code-length check, returndata returned as bytes; reaches precompiles

O40.recordedClaim: `rawCall` to a code-less non-precompile address succeeds with empty returndata

O41.recordedClaim: A reverting `rawCall` target reverts `RawCallFailed(target, data)`; the reason is lost; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

O42.recordedClaim: `code(account)` returns the full runtime code; a code-less account yields empty bytes

O43.recordedClaim: `concat(parts, delimiter)` joins in order with the delimiter between consecutive parts, preserves empty parts, empty `parts` yields empty bytes

O44.recordedClaim: `slice(data, start, len)` returns the window or reverts `SliceOutOfBounds(start, len, dataLength)`, including when `start + len` would overflow

O45.recordedClaim: `sliceRange` has JS Array.slice semantics (signed, clamped, end exclusive, empty when inverted) and never reverts

O47.recordedClaim: `stringSlice`: validates the whole input as UTF-8 first, takes the clamped signed byte range, reverts `InvalidUtf8` at a boundary that splits a code point, empty range returns empty

O48.recordedClaim: `stringAt`: returns an ASCII byte; `InvalidByteIndex` out of range; `InvalidUtf8` for any byte of a multi-byte code point; validates the whole string

O49.recordedClaim: UTF-8 validation follows the Unicode well-formed table: leads C2-F4, overlong/surrogate/past-U+10FFFF refused at the second byte, bad continuation at itself, truncated at the lead; error at the first offending byte

O50.recordedClaim: `byteLen` is the raw byte length; `hash` is keccak256 of the argument

O51.recordedClaim: `hashPairSorted` is keccak256 of the ascending pair, byte-identical to OpenZeppelin MerkleProof's combiner; `foldWords` over a proof reproduces the root

O52.recordedClaim: `indexOf` enumerates nonoverlapping matches left-to-right, supports signed occurrence ordinals and returns s.length when absent; empty needles match 0..s.length.

O53.recordedClaim: For nonempty delimiters, segment j starts after match j-1 (or zero) and ends at match j (or input length); normalize negative j against matchCount+1.

O54.recordedClaim: `contains`: true iff the needle occurs; an empty needle always matches, even in empty `s`; total

O55.recordedClaim: `split`: count + 1 segments on the same enumeration as `indexOf`, empty segments preserved, `EmptyNeedle` for an empty delimiter

O56.recordedClaim: `replace`: every non-overlapping occurrence replaced; empty `repl` deletes; empty needle reverts `EmptyNeedle`

O57.recordedClaim: `toLower`/`toUpper` fold ASCII letters only; every other byte (UTF-8 units included) passes through

O58.recordedClaim: `charset` equals the All-mode byte fold with constant mask, init=1 and accumulator/element windows sharing the byte-argument offset.

O59.recordedClaim: Byte search compares complete words and masks the remaining tail bytes; it imposes no fixed gas-cost guarantee.

O60.recordedClaim: Byte/text operations retain their declared validation and overflow errors; sufficiently large inputs or outputs can exhaust resources.

O61.recordedClaim: `parseUint` is strict: `EmptyNumber` on empty input, `InvalidDecimalDigit(position, char)` outside 0-9, Panic(0x11) past 2^256 - 1, leading zeros accepted

O62.recordedClaim: `toString(uint256)` renders without leading zeros; `toString(parseUint(s))` normalizes and `parseUint(toString(v)) == v`

O63.recordedClaim: `parseInt`: optional + or -, `EmptyNumber` on empty input or a bare sign, `InvalidDecimalDigit` elsewhere, Panic(0x11) outside int256, "-2^255" accepted

O64.recordedClaim: `toString(int256)`: leading minus for negatives, no plus, no leading zeros; int256.min renders correctly

O65.recordedClaim: `parseUnits` accepts an optional sign, at most one decimal point and at least one digit; precision is <=77 and overflow raises Panic(0x11).

O66.recordedClaim: `parseUnits` rounds dropped fractional digits: Trunc toward zero, Floor toward -inf, Ceil toward +inf

O67.recordedClaim: `parseUnitsUnsigned`: accepts a leading +, rejects - with `InvalidDecimalDigit` at 0 (negative zero included), Panic(0x11) outside uint256

O68.recordedClaim: Unsigned `formatUnits` emits canonical decimal text with trimmed fractional zeros; parsing that text at the same precision recovers the value.

O70.recordedClaim: `encode(types, values)` is runtime abi.encode from canonical component encodings (static: w * 32 bytes; dynamic: [0x20][tail]), nested dynamics spliced verbatim, returned raw without an envelope

O72.recordedClaim: `encodeBytes` returns the same tuple payload inside a bytes envelope

O73.recordedClaim: `encode`/`encodeBytes` hold static words to their narrow type's range, as solc's decoder does

O74.recordedClaim: A dirty word spliced into a typed Operations parameter (e.g. address) fails the callee's ABI decoding and surfaces as `CallFailed`

O75.recordedClaim: Operations' own panics (`rpow` base 0, `expWad` overflow, signed magnitude overflow) are byte-identical to the compiler's Panic reverts

O76.recordedClaim: An Operations call made through the core's `read` IS the composition; judged via a STATIC_CALL at the core

O79.recordedClaim: Operations' runtime bytecode fits EIP-170 (24,576 bytes)

O80.recordedClaim: Arithmetic helpers use the configured OpenZeppelin Math dependency; modular powers use their own checked-size precompile path.

O81.recordedClaim: A string operand's resolved envelope splices into `hash`/`toLower`/`byteLen` so they see the decoded payload

L1.recordedClaim: foldWords is a left fold: accumulator window rewritten with the running accumulator, element window with each word, final accumulator returned

L2.recordedClaim: foldRange substitutes the index 0..n-1; foldBytes substitutes the byte VALUE as a word

L3.recordedClaim: FoldExit: Full scans all, Any stops at first nonzero accumulator, All at first zero; final accumulator returned either way

L4.recordedClaim: Early exit never touches later elements, so a would-revert application past the exit point never happens

L5.recordedClaim: Window stamping: accumulator first, then element windows in supplied order; element wins over accumulator on overlap, later element windows win on mutual overlap; bytes outside windows stay pristine template

L6.recordedClaim: Empty fold domain validates template windows, then returns init without inspecting or calling the target

L7.recordedClaim: Window offsets must leave room for a 32-byte word (LambdaOffsetOutOfBounds(offset, templateLength)), accumulator window included, checked before any call

L8.recordedClaim: A code-less lambda/callback target (precompiles included) reverts InvalidCallbackTarget

L9.recordedClaim: Target code is checked lazily: an empty input never touches the target

L10.recordedClaim: A lambda revert reverts with CallbackFailed(operation, index, other, target, callData, reason), reason preserved; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

L11.recordedClaim: A word lambda returning other than exactly 32 bytes reverts InvalidCallbackResult(op, index, 0, target)

L12.recordedClaim: filterWords keeps the ELEMENTS whose lambda returns canonical 1, in order; any result other than 0/1 reverts InvalidCallbackResult

L13.recordedClaim: mapWords returns the lambda's word per element, same word count; empty payload returns empty without touching the target

L14.recordedClaim: Every word operation (folds, map/filter, wordIndexOf, reverse, zip, unzip, sort, unique, sum) rejects a non-multiple-of-32 payload with UnalignedWords(length)

L16.recordedClaim: `iotaWords` allocates n*32 bytes; multiplication overflow, allocator limits and exhaustion can fail for sufficiently large n.

L17.recordedClaim: wordIndexOf returns the least matching index, or the word COUNT as not-found sentinel

L19.recordedClaim: zipWords interleaves a0,b0,a1,b1...; different word counts revert WordCountMismatch(aWords, bWords)

L20.recordedClaim: unzipWords lane 0/1 is zipWords' inverse; lane > 1 reverts InvalidLane; odd count leaves the extra word in lane 0

L21.recordedClaim: sortWords returns the payload sorted ascending as UNSIGNED words (a permutation)

L22.recordedClaim: Word sorting is stable. Callback sorting has stable ties and global order only for comparisons coherent with a total preorder.

L23.recordedClaim: Merge sort uses O(n log n) algorithmic comparisons/moves and O(n) scratch space; callback cost and EVM gas are separate.

L24.recordedClaim: Signed sort is the three-node recipe: flip sign bit via mapWords(bitXor), sortWords, flip back

L25.recordedClaim: sumWords is the checked sum; overflow reverts Panic(0x11)

L27.recordedClaim: uniqueWords keeps the first occurrence of each word in original order (ordered=false, O(n^2)) and only drops adjacent duplicates when ordered=true (grouping trusted, not validated)

L31.recordedClaim: An out-of-range FoldExit is refused by the ABI decoder with an empty revert

L32.recordedClaim: Collection operations can fail through validation, callback errors, checked arithmetic, allocation or exhaustion; no universal resource-safety guarantee applies.

L33.recordedClaim: Hostile callback modes retain ordinary declared failures; a failed exhausted callback or exact reserved signal raises `SubcallOutOfGas()` before wrapping

L34.recordedClaim: packArray assembles canonical abi.encode(T[]) from canonical abi.encode(T) elements; unpackArray is its inverse

L35.recordedClaim: packArray/unpackArray validate the whole input; non-canonical encodings revert AbiCodec InvalidValue at the offending offset

L37.recordedClaim: Traversals validate visited elements; descriptors and callback preparation are still checked on empty input.

L38.recordedClaim: mapValues applies the callback in order and validates each result as canonical outputType (InvalidCallbackResult otherwise)

L39.recordedClaim: filterValues keeps the original encodings of matching values, in order

L40.recordedClaim: Predicate callbacks must return exactly one word holding canonical 0/1, else InvalidCallbackResult (stricter than core `cond`)

L41.recordedClaim: foldValues is a left fold, accumulator in slot `first`, element in `second`; empty input returns `initial`; no early exit

L42.recordedClaim: foldValues validates each result as canonical accumulatorType and `initial` too

L43.recordedClaim: `sortValues` interprets comparator results as signed words: <=0 selects the left occurrence, >0 the right; successful output preserves all occurrences.

L44.recordedClaim: Callback consistency is trusted, not checked; inconsistent answers may change ordering/selection, and failed or invalid replies still revert.

L45.recordedClaim: `uniqueValues` greedily compares retained values to each candidate. First equality-class representatives require coherent equivalence replies; ordered mode additionally requires grouped classes.

L46.recordedClaim: flattenValues concatenates inner arrays in order, one level, validating every element

L48.recordedClaim: sliceValues has JavaScript Array.slice semantics (signed, clamped, end exclusive, empty when end <= start) and never reverts on the range

L49.recordedClaim: sliceValues validates only the selected elements

L50.recordedClaim: indexOfValues returns the first index whose equality callback (element in `first`, needle in `second`) is true, else type(uint256).max; needle validated

L51.recordedClaim: anyValues/allValues/findValues: any false and all true on empty; find returns first index or max; each stops at the first decisive element

L52.recordedClaim: zipValues pairs element-wise into canonical (leftType,rightType) values; a dynamic side gets the 0x20 envelope, a static pair is bare words; LengthMismatch on unequal lengths

L53.recordedClaim: unzipValues is zipValues' inverse; lane > 1 reverts InvalidLane; BOTH sides validated even when the requested lane is well formed; envelope, offsets and exact consumption checked

L54.recordedClaim: Callback slots/counts must match a tuple descriptor; malformed syntax raises `InvalidTypeDescriptor`, while structural mismatch raises `InvalidCallback`.

L55.recordedClaim: Constant slots validated once up front against their component types; substituted values validated at every binding against the slot type

L56.recordedClaim: Calldata is rebuilt per application, so dynamic, variable-length slots (middle slot, string accumulator) are safe

L57.recordedClaim: Every lambda/callback application is a staticcall, so callbacks cannot have side effects

L58.recordedClaim: Expression callbacks: non-empty `expression` makes the call target.evaluateEncoded(expression, boundSlots), selector ignored; Parameter nodes read the bound slots

L59.recordedClaim: An expression failure surfaces as NodeCallFailed wrapped inside CallbackFailed; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

L60.recordedClaim: Expression caches last one evaluation/callback invocation; sharing across collection iterations is not implied.

L61.recordedClaim: The locally declared IExpressions.evaluateEncoded selector matches Expressions'

L62.recordedClaim: Collections is stateless and view/pure only

L63.recordedClaim: Collections runtime fits under the EIP-170 limit (and Operations plus Collections together would not)

E1.recordedClaim: A reference must point strictly backwards; a forward or self reference reverts `InvalidReference(node, ref)` before evaluation

E2.recordedClaim: A Parameter node reads `parameters[index]`; an index past the supplied parameters reverts `InvalidReference(node, index)`

E3.recordedClaim: A Parameter whose `data` is not exactly one word reverts `InvalidNode(node)`

E4.recordedClaim: A `result` index past the last node reverts `InvalidNode(result)`

E5.recordedClaim: Each kind carries an exact reference count (Call >= 1, Select 3, TryOrElse/ProbeCall 2, Wrap/IsValid 1, Literal/Parameter/Resolve 0, Array/Tuple any), else `InvalidNode(node)`

E6.recordedClaim: ProbeCall calldata must reference a bytes-typed node and validate canonically; malformed Resolve/evaluateEncoded payloads can still revert without data.

E7.recordedClaim: Every node's `valueType` is parsed up front (unreachable nodes included), `InvalidTypeDescriptor` otherwise

E8.recordedClaim: Every cold evaluated node is validated against valueType before caching; cached values originated from successful validation.

E10.recordedClaim: Evaluation is on demand from `result`: only reachable nodes execute

E11.recordedClaim: Successful node values are cached; failed guarded attempts discard cache changes, so their work may execute again.

E12.recordedClaim: Select judges the first word of the condition: nonzero picks `refs[1]`, zero `refs[2]`; a multi-word condition counts only its first word

E13.recordedClaim: Only the chosen Select branch executes (lazy)

E14.recordedClaim: Successfully validated node values occupy at least one ABI word, so Select can read their first word.

E15.recordedClaim: TryOrElse yields the attempt on success and the fallback on any ordinary failure; IsValid returns abi.encode(success); exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

E17.recordedClaim: Values memoized inside a successful guarded attempt are kept for the rest of the evaluation

E18.recordedClaim: A failed guarded attempt discards its cache changes

E19.recordedClaim: Only typed internal guarded calls can supply a cache; outside callers fail NotSelf and generic self-targeted guarded calls are forbidden.

E20.recordedClaim: Call nodes construct canonical argument tuples and staticcall from Expressions; descriptor validity does not prove external target semantics.

E21.recordedClaim: A Call or ProbeCall target word must be a clean address, else `InvalidNode(node)`

E22.recordedClaim: A code-less call target reverts `InvalidTarget(node, target)` (Call, Resolve's core, evaluateEncoded self-call)

E23.recordedClaim: A reverting node call reverts `NodeCallFailed(node, target, callData, reason)` with the target's reason intact; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

E24.recordedClaim: A Resolve node's value is `core.resolve(InputParam)` on `expression.core`, inline constraints enforced, validated as the node's type

E25.recordedClaim: Malformed Resolve node data can produce ABI-decoder bare reverts, allocation panics or resource failures before the core call.

E26.recordedClaim: ProbeCall: the target must revert (`DidNotRevert(target, callData)`); a nonzero selector must match the reason's first four bytes and is stripped, else `UnexpectedRevertData(expected, actual)` with `actual` zero under four bytes; a zero selector returns the whole reason; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

E27.recordedClaim: A code-less ProbeCall target yields empty bytes with a zero selector and `UnexpectedRevertData(expected, 0)` with a nonzero one

E28.recordedClaim: ProbeCall runs in Expressions' own frame, so a dynamic reason survives intact and word-aligned after stripping; an argument-less error yields empty bytes

E29.recordedClaim: Expressions' `DidNotRevert`, `UnexpectedRevertData` and local `ICore.resolve` share the core's selectors

E30.recordedClaim: Wrap yields the referenced value as one bytes envelope, abi.encode(bytes)

E31.recordedClaim: An Array node packs its referenced values as a canonical `T[]` of element type `arguments`

E32.recordedClaim: A Tuple node assembles one canonical tuple value; a dynamic tuple gets its leading 0x20 offset word

E33.recordedClaim: A Call or Tuple node whose value count differs from its descriptor reverts `ComponentCountMismatch`

E34.recordedClaim: Empty argument tuples are special-cased for call construction; `()` is not a valid node valueType.

E35.recordedClaim: `evaluate` returns the result node's value raw, so an evaluation nests as an operand like the value it computes

E36.recordedClaim: `evaluateEncoded` decodes an Expression and evaluates it through a self-call, returning the raw result under that call context.

E37.recordedClaim: A failure inside `evaluateEncoded` surfaces as `NodeCallFailed(0, expressions, callData, reason)` wrapping the inner error, which Collections reports through `CallbackFailed`; exhaustion and the exact reserved signal propagate instead (C69)

E38.recordedClaim: Malformed `evaluateEncoded` payloads can produce ABI-decoder bare reverts, allocation panics or resource failures before graph evaluation.

E39.recordedClaim: An out-of-range `Kind` never reaches the code: solc's decoder reverts without data

E40.recordedClaim: Malformed graphs/payloads can produce declared errors or decoder bare reverts; checked arithmetic and execution-resource failures remain possible.

E41.recordedClaim: Every evaluate/evaluateEncoded call initializes a fresh cache; traversal callbacks evaluate independently.

E42.recordedClaim: Each node valueType shape is parsed during admission and reused during validation; recursive canonical validation still walks its contents.

E47.recordedClaim: Collections reaches Expressions through a local `IExpressions` whose selector matches `evaluateEncoded`

E48.recordedClaim: Errors identify the node by index (InvalidNode, InvalidReference, InvalidTarget, NodeCallFailed)

E49.recordedClaim: Graph/tree value and error equivalence requires history-independent primitive results and guard classification in matching call contexts; call counts and gas need not match.

R1.recordedClaim: A release requires compiled artifacts, metadata, CREATE2 predictions, SDK addresses and runtime fixtures to agree; source edits require a coordinated rebuild.

R2.recordedClaim: Execution requires the configured Cancun-compatible EVM/compiler semantics, supported environmental observations and correct used precompiles.

R3.recordedClaim: A CREATE2 prediction does not establish deployment or matching code on any particular public chain.
